brief.greeting: Good morning. Your inbox just got a kernel upgrade and a bug tracker that lives inside Git.

stories.headline: Two new Linux stable kernels land Friday
stories.body: **Stable releases, no surprises:** Greg Kroah‑Hartman shipped 7.2.8 and 6.18.54, each packing a batch of critical fixes for distro maintainers. The updates span core subsystems and driver patches, so your servers and dev boards stay patched without a reboot frenzy.
stories.why: Staying on the latest stable kernels reduces exposure to known exploits and crashes.

stories.headline: Git‑bug brings offline bug tracking to repos
stories.body: **Bug reports, now version‑controlled:** Git‑bug embeds a distributed, offline‑first tracker directly inside any Git repo, letting you file and close issues without a separate server. It syncs via normal Git pushes, so the history stays immutable and portable.
stories.why: You can manage bugs alongside code, eliminating a third‑party tracker for small teams.

stories.headline: Proaction claims 60% sales lift with Codex stack
stories.body: **AI‑powered dev boost:** Proaction reports a 60% jump in sales and saves over 75 hours by using Codex, GPT‑Live‑1, and GPT‑6 Astra for its fleet‑management codebase. The tools auto‑generated boilerplate and caught bugs before they shipped.
stories.why: Seeing real ROI from LLMs shows they’re ready for production pipelines.

quick_hits.text: **Security:** Friday patches hit AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, and more.
**Summit:** Git 3.0 and LLM tooling discussed at 2026 contributors’ meetup.
**SQL Doom:** Hackaday shows how to code a DOOM engine in SQL.
**Runner images:** GitHub Actions now offers official CI images.
**Thrift:** Apache’s cross‑language RPC framework climbs trending list.

brief.sign_off: Catch you tomorrow – keep those kernels clean.

highlights.title: Security updates for Friday
highlights.summary: Friday security updates were released for multiple Linux distributions, covering kernel, libraries, and applications across AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, Slackware, and SUSE.
highlights.detail: Updates include critical components such as OpenSSL, PostgreSQL, and various firmware packages. Administrators should apply them promptly to mitigate disclosed vulnerabilities.

highlights.title: Git-bug: Distributed, offline-first bug tracker embedded in Git
highlights.summary: Git-bug is a distributed, offline‑first bug tracker that is embedded directly within Git repositories.
highlights.detail: The tool enables developers to manage issues without a separate server, syncing bug data through normal Git operations. It is positioned as a lightweight alternative to traditional issue trackers.

highlights.title: Proaction boosts sales 60% and saves 75+ hours with Codex
highlights.summary: Proaction reports a 60% sales increase and saves over 75 hours using Codex, GPT‑Live‑1, and GPT‑6 Astra for fleet‑management development.
highlights.detail: The company attributes faster build and operation cycles to the AI models, allowing quicker product releases. The reported gains combine both revenue growth and operational efficiency, though exact cost savings are not disclosed.

highlights.title: A summary from the 2026 Git Contributors' Summit
highlights.summary: Johannes Schindelin posted a summary of the 2026 Git Contributors' Summit, covering Git 3.0, security processes, documentation, the pluggable object database, and LLM usage.
highlights.detail: The summit highlighted ongoing work to modernize Git's architecture and integrate AI assistance into development workflows. Discussions also addressed improving security review pipelines and expanding documentation.

highlights.title: Two stable kernels for Friday
highlights.summary: Greg Kroah-Hartman released Linux kernel stable versions 7.2.8 and 6.18.54, both containing numerous important fixes.
highlights.detail: Both kernels address bugs across multiple subsystems, improving security and stability. Users of distributions that track these stable branches are advised to upgrade promptly to benefit from the patches.

items.title: Abusing SQL to Play DOOM
items.summary: A Hackaday article explores using SQL as a programming language to implement a DOOM engine.
items.detail: The piece demonstrates that SQL's procedural extensions can express game logic, showing a novel, though impractical, use case for database queries beyond data management.

items.title: Easy Ways Sink a Hardware Startup
items.summary: Hackaday outlines five common mistakes that can cause hardware startups to fail, based on observations by Ryan Walker.
items.detail: The article revisits earlier advice, emphasizing disciplined engineering, realistic budgeting, and clear market focus as critical factors for early-stage hardware companies.

items.title: actions/runner-images
items.summary: GitHub Actions provides official runner images for CI workflows.
items.detail: These images include pre‑installed runtimes and tools, allowing developers to run jobs without building custom environments, and are updated regularly to include security patches.

items.title: anthropics/claude-code-action
items.summary: The anthropics/claude-code-action repository offers a GitHub Action to run Claude code generation.
items.detail: Integrating this action enables automated code suggestions within CI pipelines, leveraging Anthropic's Claude model for code completion tasks.

items.title: apache/thrift
items.summary: The apache/thrift repository hosts the Apache Thrift cross-language RPC framework written in C++.
items.detail: Thrift facilitates efficient communication between services written in different languages, providing code generation and serialization utilities for high‑performance distributed systems.

items.title: base/base

items.detail: The repository aggregates the essential libraries and utilities for the Base platform, aiming to simplify setup and integration for developers working with the ecosystem.

items.summary: BMAD-METHOD is a Python project proposing a new approach to agile AI-driven development.
items.detail: The repository outlines a methodology intended to accelerate AI development cycles, emphasizing flexibility and rapid iteration, though specific performance metrics are not provided.

items.title: bootandy/dust
items.summary: Dust is a Rust implementation of a more intuitive disk usage analyzer, similar to du.
items.detail: Designed to improve usability over traditional du, dust offers clearer output and faster performance by leveraging Rust's safety and concurrency features.
